clue.text: Zeppelin tune, then leader to smoke joint!

parts.note: an air is a melody or tune

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, taken here from smoke

parts.note: the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: An excitable note about a Led Zeppelin song followed by the band's frontman lighting up a spliff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Zeppelin' and 'joint' play on the rock band and a cannabis cigarette; here Zeppelin is the airship and the joint is the hip.
explanation.definitionFit: A Zeppelin is a rigid German dirigible, a kind of lighter-than-air craft.

clue.text: God upset, consumed by a weakness, greed

indicators.note: consumed by means the god goes inside the following pieces

parts.note: a vice is a moral failing or weakness

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the god's name is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: A deity overturned by his own failing: avarice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' suits a down clue, where reading upwards turns the god's name over.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is an extreme desire for wealth, one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: More willing to use exit in back

indicators.note: in places the exit word inside the back word

parts.note: the rear is the back
to die is to exit life

explanation.surface: Someone keener to use the rear exit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exit' looks like a door; here it is the verb meaning to pass away.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready can mean willing or inclined, so readier is more willing.

clue.text: What could create hard border?

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
an edge is a border

explanation.surface: A political question about what would bring back a hard border.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a hedge creates a boundary between fields.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedge is a row of shrubs planted as a boundary.

clue.text: Fruit pulp, zest only, in long drink

parts.note: to pine is to long for

indicators.note: in places the peel of pulp inside the drink

parts.note: ale is a drink

indicators.note: zest is the outer peel, so only the outside letters of pulp

explanation.surface: A recipe: fruit pulp and zest added to a tall drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'zest only' means just the skin of the word pulp, its two outside letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A pineapple is a large tropical fruit with spiky skin.

clue.text: Polished losing gladiator's first sword

indicators.note: losing tells us a letter is dropped from the word before it

parts.note: a cut-glass accent is a refined, polished upper-class one

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of gladiator's

explanation.surface: A shiny blade that the beaten gladiator surrenders first.
explanation.walkthrough: CUT-GLASS, meaning refined or polished, loses the G that starts 'gladiator's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlass is a short curved sword, once favoured by sailors and pirates.

clue.text: Court accepts the man's case

indicators.note: accepts means the court letters take in the next piece

parts.note: the man's is he's, the man is

explanation.surface: A judge agrees to hear a man's lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks legal beside 'Court'; it is a box or trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A chest is a large strong box or case for storage.

clue.text: Novel heroine embraces rustic new body

indicators.note: embraces means the heroine's name wraps round the next pieces

parts.note: Tess of the d'Urbervilles is Thomas Hardy's heroine
a hick is an unsophisticated rustic

explanation.surface: A romance heroine hugs a country boy's young body.
explanation.definitionFit: Body can mean density or substance, as in a wine or sauce with body.

clue.text: Close shaven, cutting head

indicators.note: cutting the head removes the first letter

parts.note: shaven means hairless

explanation.surface: A close shave by a barber, trimming a scalp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' looks like part of 'close shave'; it means stuffy and humid.
explanation.definitionFit: Close weather is muggy, with little fresh air to breathe.

clue.text: Oddly sick ally dreads getting very heated

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third, fifth and further odd letters of the words

explanation.surface: An ill friend fears running a fever.
explanation.definitionFit: Scalded describes being burnt by hot liquid or steam, so heated to an extreme.

clue.text: Zeppelin possibly playing, showing wildness

parts.note: Led Zeppelin is an example of a band, so 'a band'
a show or record that is playing is on

explanation.surface: Led Zeppelin on stage, performing with characteristic wild energy.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'possibly' marks Zeppelin as just one example of a band.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandon as a noun is uninhibited freedom, as in dancing with wild abandon.

clue.text: Ceremony involving King in each country

indicators.note: in places the ceremony with its king inside the abbreviation for each
involving means the ceremony word takes in the king letter

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony
R is short for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A coronation-style rite with a monarch in every nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Eritrea is a nation in the Horn of Africa, on the Red Sea coast.

clue.text: One can shout, welcoming European traveller

parts.note: the Roman numeral I stands for one

indicators.note: welcoming means the can-and-shout pair takes in another letter

parts.note: a tin is a can
to rant is to shout or rave

explanation.surface: Someone who can raise a cheer to greet a visitor from the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' looks like a verb of ability; it is a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: An itinerant is a person who travels from place to place, with no fixed home.

clue.text: Audibly cry out for massage

indicators.note: audibly tells us the answer is spoken the same as another word

parts.note: to cry out for something is to need it

explanation.surface: Begging loudly for a rubdown.
explanation.definitionFit: To knead is to work muscles with the hands, as a masseur does.

clue.text: Discovers taking top off makes money

indicators.note: taking the top off removes the first letter of the across word

parts.note: to learn something is to discover it

explanation.surface: Someone finds out that stripping off pays.
explanation.walkthrough: LEARNS drops its opening L.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn is to receive income in return for work, so it means making money.

clue.text: Play for time protecting whole wicket

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a batsman ... by playing purely defensively to guard the stumps

explanation.surface: A batter blocks every ball to save the match.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the wicket is the set of stumps the batter defends.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonewalling means blocking progress, by delaying tactics or by dour defensive batting.

clue.text: Stewardesses so polite holding back berserk

indicators.note: back means the held letters are read in reverse order
holding means the answer is held within the run of words

explanation.surface: Courteous cabin crew restraining a passenger who has gone wild.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'stewardesSES SO Polite' from right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone possessed acts as if in the grip of a demon, wildly out of control.

clue.text: Up, feel great about University, occasionally

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the whole is read from the bottom
about means the feel-great letters go around the university

parts.note: to seem is to feel, as in it seems right
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology
OS is outsize, a great clothing size

explanation.surface: Students now and then feel elated about their university.
explanation.walkthrough: MIT goes inside SEEMOS after SE, giving SEMITEMOS, which 'Up' reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Sometimes and occasionally both mean now and then.

clue.text: Oil part in silent power turning over

indicators.note: in puts the part word inside the reversed string
turning over means the silent-plus-power string is read backwards

parts.note: mute means silent
P is the physics symbol for power
a role is a part in a play

explanation.surface: A walk-on role in a silent film about the oil industry's power shifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning over' acts on both 'silent' and 'power' together, before the part goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Petroleum is crude oil, the mineral oil pumped from underground.

clue.text: Shakespearean character's endless boom …

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: Prospero is the magician in The Tempest; the 's is read as is

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare character's never-ending roar, continuing into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to the next clue for the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: To boom is to thrive or flourish, as an economy prospers.

clue.text: … cheers Shakespeare's old habits

parts.note: ta and cheers are both British ways to say thanks
Shakespeare is the Bard, so Shakespeare's is the Bard's

explanation.surface: Raising a toast to Shakespeare's old ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habits' looks like customs; it means garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabards are sleeveless tunics worn by medieval knights and heralds, a kind of old garment.

clue.text: Initially serves, and launches volley on volley

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letters of the following five words

explanation.surface: A tennis rally: serving, then hitting one volley after another.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a simultaneous discharge of guns, a volley of fire.

clue.text: Thinnest and smallest eating nectarine's rind

indicators.note: eating means the smallest word takes in the next piece

parts.note: least means smallest

indicators.note: rind is the outside, so the outer letters of nectarine's

explanation.surface: A dieter, slimmest of all, eats only nectarine peel.
explanation.definitionFit: Leanest means having the least fat, so the thinnest.

clue.text: Lover seems to be taking control

indicators.note: taking means the words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: A partner appears to be seizing power in the relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is in 'lOVER SEEms'.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to supervise or direct, so to control.

clue.text: Game over with vacant mob about

parts.note: O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over

indicators.note: vacant empties the word mob, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: The match is finished, the crowd having emptied out.
explanation.definitionFit: Ombre is an old card game for three players, popular in the 17th and 18th centuries.

clue.text: 'American Way' missing Republican, lacking a will

indicators.note: missing means a letter is removed from the highway word

parts.note: an interstate is a US highway, an American way or road

explanation.surface: A dig at the American Way without the Republicans, implying the country has lost its resolve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American Way' looks like the national ideal; it is a road.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dies intestate has made no valid testament for their estate.

clue.text: Stuff wasting time for offspring!

indicators.note: wasting means the time letter is lost

parts.note: tissue is stuff or fabric

explanation.surface: Exasperation at children who waste time.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a formal word for children or descendants, as in died without issue.

clue.text: River wave, sort of catching tide finally

indicators.note: catching means the wave word holds the next letter

parts.note: a sine wave is one sort of wave

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of tide

explanation.surface: A river wave catching the tide at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Seine is the river flowing through Paris.

clue.text: Snappers circling Queen start to harass, maybe

indicators.note: circling means the photographers surround the next pieces

parts.note: paps, short for paparazzi, are press photographers who snap celebrities

indicators.note: start to means the opening letter of harass

explanation.surface: Paparazzi surround the monarch and might begin to pester her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snappers' looks like dogs or fish; it is the press photographers known as paps.

clue.text: Misses relief found in Gents, commonly

indicators.note: found in puts the relief word inside

explanation.surface: Someone misses the relief to be had in the men's room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Misses' looks like a verb but is the plural of Miss, unmarried young women.
explanation.definitionFit: Maidens are young unmarried women, addressed as Miss.

clue.text: Break down and do all this again

definitions.meaning: to separate into constituent parts, as a chemist or analyst does
read as ..., meaning to solve the puzzle a second time

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a joke on the crossword itself: re-solve it.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolve means analyse into parts; re-solve means work out the clues once more.

clue.text: Singular couple adopting little darling

indicators.note: adopting means the first pieces take in the next word

parts.note: S is the grammar abbreviation for singular
to tie is to couple or join

explanation.surface: An unusual pair take in a tiny child, their little darling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singular couple' reads as an odd pair, but splits into two separate pieces.
